## Audit Test Suite Refactoring

**Summary:** Refactor `tests/test_triage_audit.py` to target the new descriptor-driven handler API. Add new test files for `AuditResult` dataclass/parser and handler unit tests. Maintain coverage for cooldown (caller concern), blocked items, Discord integration, and auto-completion.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Existing 13 test scenarios from `tests/test_triage_audit.py` are preserved or intentionally replaced with equivalent coverage targeting the new handler API
- [ ] New tests for `AuditResult` parsing (>=5 samples: pass, fail, malformed, empty, multi-AC)
- [ ] New tests for each handler covering: from-state validation, invariant evaluation, state transitions, error cases
- [ ] New tests for extended auto-completion checks (PR merge, CI status, PR comments, children, deps)
- [ ] All external calls mocked (`wl`, `opencode run`, `gh pr view`, `gh api`)
- [ ] Test coverage for audit-related code paths >= prior level as measured by `pytest --cov`
- [ ] Tests verify behavioral parity with descriptor definitions (not hardcoded heuristics)

## Minimal Implementation

- Refactor `tests/test_triage_audit.py` to target new handler functions/classes
- New `tests/test_audit_result.py` for AuditResult dataclass and parser
- New `tests/test_audit_handlers.py` for handler-specific unit tests (if not covered by refactored file)
- Update mocking patterns to match new API (protocols, adapters)

## Dependencies

- SA-0MM8W4FQR0UY1NHQ (AuditResult dataclass)
- SA-0MM8W553C1WK7JE5 (audit_result handler)
- SA-0MM8W5EXT1BXC7PB (audit_fail handler)
- SA-0MM8W5U8C0QGGXTD (close_with_audit handler)
- SA-0MM8W69L91DJQY50 (routing — partial block for integration tests only)

## Deliverables

- Refactored test files
- New test files as needed
- Coverage report verification

## Reference Files

- `tests/test_triage_audit.py` — existing tests (1178 lines, 13 tests)
- `docs/workflow/test-plan.md` — TC-DL test specifications for audit scenarios
- `docs/workflow/examples/02-audit-failure.md` — audit failure flow reference

## Problem

When a new project is created (or an existing one initialized) with an AGENTS.md, the current installer/template behavior emits the full duplicated instruction set as a local file. This is how the four sibling projects ended up with large local AGENTS.md files that duplicate the global one (see SA-0MSITKHPW002XG4G, SA-0MSITKOXI007XD4N).

## User story

As a developer creating a new project, I want the AGENTS.md installer to emit only the canonical global-reference structure so new projects never start by duplicating the global rules.

## Desired change

Improve the tooling/template that creates AGENTS.md for a project so the generated local file contains only the canonical structure (as adopted by SorraAgents itself in SA-0MSIUUYRD002GC8W):

    ## Global agent guidance

    Read the global agent instructions at ~/.pi/agent/AGENTS.md — they define the core principles, the Worklog (wl) work-item workflow, and the coding disciplines that apply to every project.

    ## Project-specific guidance

    (project-specific rules are added by the project owner here, never by copying the global file)

- Locate the installer/template mechanism (search scripts, wl/pi project init, templates dir, .pi scaffolding) and change the emitted template.
- The canonical structure is emitted by default; project-specific rules are added by the project owner on top, never by copying the global file.
- If the installer supports an option to copy the global file (e.g. for offline/standalone use), keep it as an explicit opt-in.
- Coordinate with the Worklog side: ContextHub wl init should delegate agent-guidance/workflow setup to the SorraAgents install rather than duplicating it (tracked in ContextHub work item WL-0MSIXMKOX0052514).

## Acceptance criteria

1. The installer/template that creates AGENTS.md now emits exactly the canonical structure above (## Global agent guidance reference + ## Project-specific guidance placeholder).
2. Creating a fresh project (or re-running init) produces an AGENTS.md whose content is the canonical structure, not a copy of the global file.
3. Existing behavior for projects with custom local rules is unaffected (they keep their local rules below the reference line).
4. Any docs describing the installer and the global-vs-project AGENTS.md split are updated.
5. Full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Key Files

- TBD at plan time: search for AGENTS.md templates/installers (e.g. ~/.pi/agent/ scaffolding, pi init, project setup scripts). Candidate locations: ~/.pi/agent/settings.json, /usr/local/lib/node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/ (pi's own project init), any templates/ dirs in ~/.pi/agent/.

## Related work

- related-to:SA-0MSISKM8F004NW1U (audit session context reduction)
- related-to:SA-0MSITKHPW002XG4G (SorraAgents AGENTS.md dedup)
- related-to:SA-0MSITKOXI007XD4N (sibling projects AGENTS.md dedup)
- ContextHub: wl init delegation to SorraAgents install (WL-0MSIXMKOX0052514)
data.title: AGENTS.md installer: emit single reference line for new projects

## Summary

The F6 regression gate (AC3 of SA-0MSLK7XNZ00366YY) is enforced via the pytest suite (`tests/test_context_budget_gate.py`), but the `.githooks/pre-push` v2 hook containing the context-budget gate is NOT wired into the active hooks directory. The active `.git/hooks/pre-push` is a stale v1 (dated 2026-07-25, 1,038 B) containing only worklog sync, and `git config core.hooksPath` is unset. The audit (SA-0MSLK7XNZ00366YY, AC3 "adjusted") flagged this as the one enforcement gap: a push that regresses the context budget would not be blocked locally before reaching `dev`.

## Target outcome

Every `git push` to `dev` runs the context-budget gate (via the committed v2 pre-push hook), so future PRs cannot regress the ~54% context reduction without a developer actively bypassing the gate.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: The context-budget gate runs on every push in this repo — either by setting `core.hooksPath` to `.githooks/` or by installing `.githooks/pre-push` into `.git/hooks/pre-push`; verified by an end-to-end simulated push (gate present, hook fires).
- AC2: Worklog sync from the old v1 `.git/hooks/pre-push` is preserved (merged into v2 or still running) so switching hooks does not regress the sync behavior.
- AC3: `docs/dev/context-budget.md` enforcement section updated to describe the ACTIVE mechanism (hooksPath config or install command), including the `CONTEXT_BUDGET_SKIP=1` bypass and fail-open behavior when tooling is absent.
- AC4: Full test suite remains green (pytest + Node), including `tests/test_context_budget_gate.py` and the pre-push hook tests.

## Minimal implementation

- Choose mechanism: `git config core.hooksPath .githooks` (repo-level, recommended) or install the hook file.
- Verify v2 hook runs `measure_context.py --include-hidden --thresholds` on push and exits non-zero on threshold exceed.
- Confirm no double-run of worklog sync and no interference with `implement.py`/`ship` push flows.
- Update `docs/dev/context-budget.md` lines ~152-170 (enforcement instructions).

## Dependencies

- F6 (SA-0MSLK7XNZ00366YY) — gate hook file + thresholds already committed; this wires them into the active hooks.
- `.githooks/pre-push` v2 (already committed).

## Deliverables

- Active pre-push gate (hooksPath config or installed hook)
- Updated enforcement docs
- Green suite

## Notes

- Discovered during audit of SA-0MSLK7XNZ00366YY (AC3 variance, non-blocking).
- No CI exists in this repo; the pre-push hook is the intended local gate.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **SA-0MPDZDPZB00121IE** – Implement: Branch naming & policy (completed)
- **SA-0MSMT0BA7008K7NR** – [MEDIUM] /home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents/tests/test_measure_context.py:19 — Unused `noqa` directive (non-enabled: `E402`) (RUF100) (open)
- **SA-0MTXLTKFP000ZUZ8** – implement.py finish hardcodes a 600s test timeout, so repos with a >10 min suite can never pass the pre-commit gate (open)

### Repository file matches
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — matched: absent, ac1, ac2, ac3, ac4 (+105 more)
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — matched: absent, ac1, ac2, ac3, ac4 (+94 more)
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md` — matched: absent, ac2, ac3, ac4, acceptance (+85 more)

## Current state (verified 2026-09-23, plan auto-review)

The original premise is partly stale: later work has already landed most of this item.

- `core.hooksPath` **is now set** to `.githooks` in this clone (`.git/config`), so the committed `.githooks/pre-push` (**now v3**, mode 755) is the active hook. It contains the context-budget gate (`measure_context.py --include-hidden --thresholds`), branch policy, a scope-aware full-suite gate, and worklog sync (fail-open). **AC2 satisfied.**
- `scripts/install_pi.sh` sets `core.hooksPath=.githooks` idempotently (commit 6052e69c), so the wiring is reproducible for fresh clones/installs.
- `docs/dev/context-budget.md` already documents the active mechanism, `CONTEXT_BUDGET_SKIP=1`, and fail-open. **AC3 satisfied.**
- The gate currently passes: total 14017 B, exit 0, within committed thresholds. **AC4 (gate) satisfied.**

**Residual work (AC1 verification evidence):** no test performs an end-to-end *simulated push to `dev`* proving the **context-budget** gate fires and blocks on threshold exceed. `tests/unit/test-pre-push-hook.mjs` simulates pushes only for branch policy and greps the hook file for the context-budget gate; `tests/test_context_budget_gate.py` exercises `measure_context.py` directly; `tests/test_pre_push_hook_fallback.py` covers path resolution. Implementation should add the missing simulated-push test (test-first) and confirm AC1 end-to-end.

**Key Files:**
- `scripts/install_pi.sh`
- `docs/dev/context-budget.md`
- `docs/dev/context-budget.thresholds.json`
- `tests/test_context_budget_gate.py`
- `tests/test_pre_push_hook_fallback.py`
- `tests/test_install_pi_hook_wiring.py`

# Skills: tag pi sessions spawned from skills with --session-id

## Problem statement

Every pi session spawned from within a skill — the audit skill's `_call_pi()` in `audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` and `run_audit_in_worktree()` in `audit/audit_pr.py` — is saved under pi's default random session ID, so when debugging an audit run it is impossible to tell which session belongs to which work item or which phase produced it. Skills should pass `--session-id` so every spawned pi session clearly identifies the work item it is for and the action being taken (e.g. `audit-{id}-{phase}-{uuid}`).

## Users

- **Producers/operators** debugging audit runs: want to identify, resume, and inspect the exact pi session for a given work item and phase (`pi --session <id>` / `/resume`).
- **Audit skill maintainers**: want session-per-call isolation (unique ID per call) so parallel/fan-out pi calls never share a session file and never re-trigger the "Cannot continue from message role: assistant" failure mode.
- **Operators of long-running systems**: want stale skill-spawned sessions pruned automatically so `~/.pi/agent/sessions/` does not grow unboundedly.

### Example user stories

- As a producer, I want each pi session spawned during an audit to carry `--session-id audit-{work_item_id}-{phase}-{short_uuid}`, so I can resume the exact session that produced a failed verdict.
- As a maintainer, I want each call to get a unique session (not a shared one), so repeated calls never append into the same session file and never hit the assistant-role continuation error that Ralph's original `--no-session` fix addressed.
- As an operator, I want `audit-*` sessions older than a retention period automatically pruned after each audit run, so the session store stays bounded.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Every pi subprocess spawned by the audit skill passes `--session-id` with a unique per-call value. `_call_pi()` in `audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` appends `--session-id <id>` to the constructed command; the value is generated in `_call_pi_and_maybe_log()` as `audit-{work_item_id}-{context}-{short_uuid}` (short uuid = `uuid4().hex[:8]`).
- [ ] `audit/audit_pr.py` `run_audit_in_worktree()` passes `--session-id audit-pr-{wl_id}-{short_uuid}` for each spawned pi call.
- [ ] Session IDs are unique per call — no two calls share a session file; session-per-call isolation means no "Cannot continue from message role: assistant" errors are introduced.
- [ ] Project-level audits (no work-item id) use a stable placeholder in the id (`audit-project-{short_uuid}` — dedupe the repeated `project` context so the id reads cleanly).
- [ ] Automatic cleanup runs at the end of an audit run (`issue` and `project` commands): session files whose names match the `audit-` prefix and whose mtime is older than the retention period (default 112 days) are pruned from the pi session directory.
- [ ] Retention is configurable via a `--session-retention-days` CLI flag on both subcommands and/or an `AUDIT_SESSION_RETENTION_DAYS` env var (flag wins).
- [ ] Cleanup is conservative: it only removes `audit-`-prefixed sessions — never other pi sessions.
- [ ] Tests verify: (a) `--session-id` appears in every constructed pi command with the expected format, (b) session ids are unique across calls, (c) cleanup prunes only stale `audit-*` files and honors the retention setting, (d) existing cmd-construction tests (e.g. `TestCallPiEnableTools`) are updated and still pass.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md`, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Follow the established Ralph session-per-call precedent (SA-0MQ6E8NCG003STJB): unique `--session-id` per call, dash-separated `{skill}-{work_item_id}-{phase}-{short_uuid}` format, conservative prefix-scoped cleanup, default retention 112 days.
- Backward compatible: `_call_pi()` gains an optional `session_id: str | None = None` parameter; when unset the command is byte-identical to today (existing direct callers/tests unaffected).
- Cleanup must never touch sessions that do not start with the `audit-` prefix.
- The audit skill's context-reduction invariants (`--no-context-files --no-skills`, self-contained prompts) are untouched.
- `CHANGELOG.md` is excluded (managed by the ship skill release pipeline).

## Existing state

- `audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` `_call_pi()` (line ~1492): `cmd = [pi_bin, "-p", "--mode", "json", "--model", model, prompt]` (+ optional `--tools`, always `--no-context-files --no-skills`). Sessions are saved under pi's default random IDs.
- `_call_pi_and_maybe_log(issue_id, context, prompt, ...)` (line ~2816) already threads `issue_id` (a work-item id, a child id, or `"project"`) and `context` (e.g. `parent`, `phase2_deep`, `child_ac_fallback`) for debug-log naming, but does not forward them to `_call_pi()`.
- `audit/audit_pr.py` `run_audit_in_worktree()` (line ~192): `cmd = ['pi', '-p', '--mode', 'json', f"/audit {wl_id}"]` — `wl_id` is in scope.
- No `--session-id` usage exists anywhere in the skill tree today.
- Session storage: pi saves to `~/.pi/agent/sessions/--<path-slug>--/` (overridable via `PI_CODING_AGENT_SESSION_DIR` / `--session-dir`); cleanup should honor the env/flag override when present.
- Existing cmd-construction tests in `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner.py` (e.g. `TestCallPiEnableTools`, ~lines 290–400) assert exact arg lists (`assert args == ["pi", "-p", ...]`) and must be updated.
- No dedicated `audit_pr.py` test file exists; add session-id coverage there or in the audit runner tests.

## Desired change

1. **`_call_pi()`**: add optional `session_id: str | None = None`; when set, append `--session-id <session_id>` to the command (before/with the context-reduction flags).
2. **`_call_pi_and_maybe_log()`**: build `session_id = f"audit-{issue_id}-{context}-{uuid4().hex[:8]}"` and forward to `_call_pi()`.
3. **`audit_pr.py`**: build `f"audit-pr-{wl_id}-{uuid4().hex[:8]}"` and append `--session-id`.
4. **Cleanup**: add a helper that scans the pi session directory (honoring `PI_CODING_AGENT_SESSION_DIR`/`--session-dir`) for files whose name starts with `audit-`, prunes those older than the retention period (default 112 days; `--session-retention-days` flag + `AUDIT_SESSION_RETENTION_DAYS` env), and logs pruned count/space. Invoke after `issue` and `project` audit commands complete.
5. **Tests**: update cmd-construction tests; add format/uniqueness assertions and cleanup tests (stale pruning, prefix scoping, retention config precedence).
6. **Docs**: update `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` and code comments documenting the session-id convention and retention.

## Key Files:

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — `_call_pi()` (~line 1492) add `--session-id` support; `_call_pi_and_maybe_log()` (~line 2816) generate `audit-{id}-{context}-{short_uuid}`; `main()`/`cmd_issue`/`cmd_project` add `--session-retention-days` + cleanup hook
- `skill/audit/audit_pr.py` — `run_audit_in_worktree()` (~line 192) add `--session-id audit-pr-{wl_id}-{short_uuid}`
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner.py` — update `TestCallPiEnableTools` cmd assertions; add session-id format/uniqueness + cleanup tests
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — document session-id convention + retention config

## Related work

- **SA-0MQ6E8NCG003STJB** — "Ralph: Use session-per-call with unique IDs instead of --no-session" (completed): direct precedent — `--session-id` per call, `{skill}-{id}-{phase}-{short_uuid}` format, 112-day retention cleanup, prefix-scoped pruning.
- **SA-0MQ533A3M003N3ER** — "Document how to execute skills via CLI" (completed): documents the session-per-call pattern for pi subprocess invocations.
- **SA-0MPFD4RWQ009AXJR** — Ralph "Cannot continue from message role: assistant" (completed): the original shared-session failure this design avoids by using unique IDs per call.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Scope creep**: session tagging could expand to every conceivable pi invocation or to a shared `pi_utils` helper refactor. Mitigation: scope is limited to the two existing spawn points; extra ideas are recorded as follow-up work items, not scope.
- **Session accumulation**: unique-per-call sessions accumulate faster than shared ones. Mitigation: retention cleanup is included in this item (default 112 days, `audit-` prefix only).
- **Filename/ID character safety**: work-item ids and context strings are filename-safe alphanumerics/dashes; no sanitization needed beyond the prefix convention.
- **Behavioral change risk**: adding a flag to every spawned command could interact with `--mode json` streaming. Mitigation: identical invocation to Ralph's proven pattern; tests assert command structure; backward-compatible default (`None`).
- **Assumption**: retention default of 112 days and the `--session-retention-days` flag naming follow the Ralph precedent; configurable via env var `AUDIT_SESSION_RETENTION_DAYS` (no config-file migration needed since the audit skill has no `.ralph.json`-style config).

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Session ID uniqueness — shared `audit_<id>` per work item (matches your `intake_<id>` example) vs Ralph-style unique per call (`audit-{id}-{phase}-{short_uuid}`)?" — Answer (user): **1b — Ralph-style unique per call** (`audit-{work_item_id}-{context}-{short_uuid}`), dash-separated. Source: interactive reply.
- Q2: "Scope — audit skill only, all current skill pi-spawn points, or audit + documented convention?" — Answer (user): **2b — all current skill pi-spawn points**. Research: a full-tree scan found exactly two spawn points, both in the audit skill: `audit_runner.py::_call_pi` and `audit_pr.py::run_audit_in_worktree`. Source: interactive reply + repo grep.
- Q3: "Cleanup — include session retention pruning in this item or keep out of scope?" — Answer (user): **include in this item**. Source: interactive reply.

## Intake Brief: Multi-agent audit/test coordination to break deadlocks

## Work item
**SA-0MTG0Y34T007ZHPF -- When multiple agents are working they can become blocked on audits/testing**

## Problem statement

When multiple agents run concurrently (herdr-dispatched implement/plan/audit panes plus manual sessions), audits and test runs contend for the same scarce host resources (local LLM slots, audit concurrency slots, CPU) and end up blocking one another. Two mechanisms interact to create a livelock/starvation pattern: (1) the herdr downtime worker only dispatches any work -- including audits -- after the local LLM has been **continuously idle >=60s with >=2 free slots**; (2) the audit runner **fails fast (0s wait)** when the host-wide audit semaphore is saturated, returning `unmet` "Audit concurrency limit reached" verdicts. Under sustained agent traffic the idle gate never opens, so audits starve; in the rare dispatch windows, concurrent audits may still collide and fail-fast, keeping items `in_review` indefinitely. Tableau-Card-Engine currently shows 28 items in `in_review` -- several 1000+ hours old (up to 4178h) -- with only 15 audit dispatches ever recorded and one audit running 8+ hours. A coordination mechanism is needed so audits proceed with bounded, prioritized concurrency independent of a strict "all traffic quiet" gate.

## Users

- **Concurrent agent herd** (herdr instances + pi panes on the same machine) running implement/plan/audit sessions -- they block on audits of their completed items.
- **Audit skill consumers** -- every completed/item-in-`in_review` work item needs a timely audit verdict to progress/close.
- **Operator (rgardler)** -- watches the worklog; a deadlocked herd produces no visible progress and wasted LLM spend.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **No fail-fast re-queue under load (north star):** under sustained concurrent agent/LLM traffic, audits no longer return `unmet` "Audit concurrency limit reached" verdicts as the *common* outcome; when the ceiling is momentarily saturated, audits wait on a bounded queue (or equivalent) rather than failing immediately. Verification: run N >= 3 concurrent audits against a busy host; zero concurrency-limit `unmet` verdicts; all audits persist real verdicts.
2. **Bounded audit turnaround (realistic start):** an `in_review` item is audited within N hours (N to be tuned) of entering that stage while multiple agents are active. Verification: seed/observe items entering `in_review` under concurrent load; 95th-percentile time-to-audit <= N. Note: turnaround is bounded within dispatch windows; the gate-opening frequency is the hard throughput ceiling (see AC3 amendment).
3. **Idle-gate decoupling for audits (amended):** *within any dispatch window*, audit dispatch/progress no longer requires a strict continuous LLM idle window; audits proceed under high agent traffic (bounded by the host-wide audit semaphore), while non-audit dispatch may retain a gentler gate. Note: the idle gate itself is unchanged (see SA-0MTG5UPBR0028K50 follow-up); this AC is satisfied by the bounded-queue mechanism ensuring audits proceed without fail-fast once a dispatch window opens.
4. **Priority ordering:** among queued/waiting audit candidates, `critical` items are audited before `high`, then age/FIFO; no item is bypassed indefinitely. Verification: deterministic ordering observed in logs/tests; the 4178h-old backlog drains.
5. **No regression to existing guards:** per-item `in_progress` claim guard, dispatched-marker exclusion, single-flight, lease/leader machinery, and test-cache read-only consumption all continue to work unchanged (see Constraints). **All related documentation updated** (audit skill reference, process_semaphore, AGENTS.md coordination section, downtime-dispatcher doc if touched). **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Single-machine scope (v1) matches herdr's current leader-election/lease model; no new network service.
- Preserve the cross-process flock semaphore primitive (no stale locks); extend semantics (bounded wait/priority/queueing) rather than replace wholesale.
- The dispatcher cannot know a work item's weight before dispatch -- fine-grained coordination belongs in the skills (audit/test) where concurrency is actually consumed; dispatcher changes should be minimal and only where they unblock (e.g., audits not gated on full idle).
- Must not destabilize working coordination machinery: leader lease (5-min TTL), 30-min check-ins, pruning, fail-closed lookups.
- Keep test execution cheap: the per-repo test cache (2h TTL) already dedupes suite runs; do not regress read-only cache consumption by audits/implement/ship.
- Respect `.gitignore`/agent-framework rules; changes to `skill/`, `command/`, `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` are tracked here, built, tested, pushed to `dev` per the global workflow.

## Plan

### Feature breakdown (5 child items, 3 vertical slices)

**Slice 1 -- Zero fail-fast + priority ordering (AC1, AC4):**
- **SA-0MTG5N7BN003D95L** (task) -- Implement shared bounded priority queue module in `skill/shared/queue.py`
- **SA-0MTG5RYH8005RQNM** (feature) -- Integrate audit runner with bounded queue (replaces fail-fast) + queue logging

**Slice 2 -- Batch drain (AC2):**
- **SA-0MTG5TP5Z008QBL5** (feature) -- Add batch drain mode (process N items per window)

**Slice 3 -- Broader scope + research (AC5):**
- **SA-0MTG5U75A001F1RG** (task) -- Extend test skill to use shared concurrency primitive
- **SA-0MTG5UPBR0028K50** (task) -- Evaluate whether idle-gate relaxation is needed (research, independent)

### Dependency graph
```
SA-0MTG5N7BN003D95L (queue module) -- foundation, no deps
  |-- SA-0MTG5RYH8005RQNM (queue integration)
  |     |-- SA-0MTG5TP5Z008QBL5 (batch drain)
  |-- SA-0MTG5U75A001F1RG (test skill)
SA-0MTG5UPBR0028K50 (gate eval) -- independent research
```

### Sequencing with related work
- **SA-0MSQIA84B005NHWC** (stale-audit detection, completed/in_review): same file area (`audit_runner.py`) but different path. This item modifies the concurrency/semaphore/launch path; SA-0MSQIA84B005NHWC works on the freshness/fingerprint path. Implement SA-0MSQIA84B005NHWC first to avoid overlapping edits.

## Key Files

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` -- `_acquire_audit_slot()` (2124), `AUDIT_LOCK_TIMEOUT` (134-135, 0s default), saturation verdict path (2796-2855); central place to add bounded wait/queue.
- `skill/shared/process_semaphore.py` -- counting semaphore (already supports `timeout>0` bounded wait; may need priority/fairness or a queue protocol, plus tests at `skill/shared/tests/`).
- `skill/shared/queue.py` -- **new**: bounded priority queue module (SA-0MTG5N7BN003D95L).
- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` -- suite run/dedup layer; candidate for the same coordination primitive if test runs contend.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` (ContextHub) -- idle gate/dispatch tiers; candidate for the audit-gate relaxation (SA-0MTG5UPBR0028K50 research).
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` (SorraAgents), `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` (ContextHub), `packages/herdr/README.md` (ContextHub), `AGENTS.md` / `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` coordination section -- docs to update.

## Related work

Potentially related work items (SorraAgents):
- SA-0MSQIA84B005NHWC -- Eliminate wasteful re-audits: stale-audit detection and cross-session audit coordination (completed/in_review, **same file area** `audit_runner.py` -- distinct concern: front freshness fast-path vs. this item's contention/queueing; sequence to avoid overlapping edits)
- SA-0MSAK2SNN005HCM5 -- Audit runner concurrency cap (completed; the existing bound)
- SA-0MSAK2P3J0065POO -- Shared cross-process semaphore module (completed; primitive to extend)
- SA-0MSGEAZMC009LHKL -- Audit skill: fail immediately when audit concurrency limit is reached (completed; the behavior this item supersedes with bounded queueing)
- SA-0MSCC02ME009EGCB -- Investigate audit concurrency TimeoutError errors (completed)
- SA-0MSAEKOQE009TEB4 -- Investigate concurrent audit fan-out causing extreme load (completed; fan-out context for ceilings)
- SA-0MSGN5OJ4002OZKY -- Cache full test-suite results for reuse across ship/audit/implement (completed)
- SA-0MSL1YS4K008HJVU -- Audit skill improvements: P1-P3 optimization backlog (open, plan_complete; watch for overlap)

ContextHub (WL-) related: downtime dispatcher leader election WL-0MST3OJ8S0001ROL, no-candidate cooldown WL-0MSI7DQL10016QYX, coordination-mode WL-0MTEZ4XZJ006Y9U7, critical-first dispatch WL-0MT3FM8VA005XBHE, idle-gate slot requirements WL-0MT32F90V008UAD2.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Should this item (a) produce an investigation+proposal that stops, (b) go straight to designing and implementing a coordination mechanism, or (c) be an epic decomposed into investigation->design->implementation children?"
  - Answer (operator/rgardler): "(b) -- go straight to designing and implementing." Source: interactive reply 2026-08-30. Implies single feature item (issueType set to `feature`), with plan stage free to decompose as needed.
- Q2: "Where should the mechanism live -- audit/test skills, herdr dispatcher, or both?"
  - Answer (operator/rgardler): "Wherever makes the most sense -- note the dispatcher may be too late as it cannot know what the work items will entail ahead of dispatch -- happy if you have a good idea."
  - Research (Map): dispatcher-side gating cannot know item weight pre-dispatch; the contention is consumed skill-side (audit semaphore, subprocess launches). Primary surface: `skill/audit` bounded prioritized queue on the existing flock semaphore; dispatcher relaxation (secondary) only to stop the strict idle gate from starving audits. Accepted as design direction; refinement at plan stage.
- Q3: "What measurable success? (a) every in_review audited within N hours, (b) zero 'concurrency limit reached' unmet verdicts, or other?"
  - Answer (operator/rgardler): "(b) is the north star goal; (a) may be a realistic start -- your guidance is required once you have evaluated."
  - Guidance (Map): north-star AC1 = zero fail-fast `unmet` verdicts under load; start-gate AC2 = bounded turnaround (initial N=24h, tuned from observed dispatch/backlog data: 28 items stuck, ~1 valid audit window per couple hours). AC1 is achievable now with bounded-wait queueing (semaphore already supports `timeout>0`); AC2 additionally needs idle-gate decoupling (AC3) so dispatches aren't rare. Priority ordering (AC4) addresses the oldest-first fairness gap.

### Plan design decisions (2026-08-30)

- Q1 (Queue protocol): **(a) File-based priority queue** (RECOMMENDED). Answer (operator/rgardler): confirmed. A shared queue directory where each waiter writes a priority+timestamp file; dispatcher reads in order (critical>high>age).
- Q2 (Idle gate): **(b) Keep gate, rely on bounded wait**. Answer (operator/rgardler): "We cannot loosen the gate, which means b is the only option. What impact does this have on ACs? What can be done?" AC3 amended: "within any dispatch window, audits proceed without fail-fast"; AC2 amended: turnaround bounded within windows, gate-opening frequency is throughput ceiling. Batch drain mode (process multiple items per window) mitigates throughput impact.
- Q3 (Scope): **(b) Shared primitive, audit first consumer, test second**. Answer (operator/rgardler): "implementation runs audits, scoping to audit only will have limited effect." The shared primitive in `skill/shared/` is consumed by audit first; test skill extended in a separate task. A follow-up research item (SA-0MTG5UPBR0028K50) evaluates whether the idle gate should be relaxed.

## Recommendations & assumptions

- **Assumption:** bounded-wait + fairness ordering on the existing semaphore is sufficient for AC1; a formal FIFO/priority queue (file-based) for AC2/AC4 is the natural extension and the core of this feature.
- **Assumption:** audits are the scarce op (tests already cached); the feature centers on audit coordination, with test coordination as a separate task.
- **Assumption:** the strict idle gate exists to protect interactive use (reserve >=1 slot); relaxation is outside v1 scope (tracked as SA-0MTG5UPBR0028K50).
- **Risk:** touching audit-runner concurrency paths regresses the many hardening fixes in that file (parent-timeout, stall detection, retry/backoff). Mitigation: surgical change in `_acquire_audit_slot`/verdict path only; run the full audit test suite.
- **Risk:** queue/prioritization adds state; a crash could strand waiting items. Mitigation: flock-based no-stale-lock design (kernel release), plus item-level retry markers so no item is lost.
- **Risk:** dispatcher-side change (if taken) interacts with herdr election/lease fail-closed logic. Mitigation: keep it minimal and documented; test tiers remain.
- **Scope-creep risk:** tuning N, backlog draining of all 28 TCE items, or building a general scheduler are separate concerns -- recorded as follow-up items if they arise, not scope here.

## Plan: changelog

- **2026-08-30 Plan skill (Map):** decomposed into 5 child items across 3 vertical slices. Design decisions: file-based priority queue (Q1a), bounded-wait replaces fail-fast with gate unchanged (Q2b), shared primitive scope includes test skill (Q3b). AC2/AC3 amended to reflect gate-stay constraint. Follow-up research item created for gate evaluation.

## Summary

`audit_runner.py issue|batch --do-not-persist` currently skips **all** persistence, including the `auditedAt` timestamp. A successful dry-run validation (`Ready to close: Yes`) therefore leaves `auditedAt` stale. `isAuditFresh(auditedAt, updatedAt)` (`auditedAt > updatedAt - 60s`, `packages/shared/src/icons.ts:250`) stays `false`, so Herdr's selection list / DOWNTIME audit tier correctly re-queues the item as a stale-audit candidate and shows the ⏳ stale-passed state.

Observed on 2026-09-01 with `SA-0MSJ1BP9K009M8MV`: validated with `--do-not-persist --force` (`Ready to close: Yes`, deep analysis completed) but stored audit remained `2026-08-11T05:13:22Z` while `updatedAt` had advanced to `2026-09-01T18:33:14Z` (delta ~21 days via `herdr-downtime` claim + comments). Herdr was correct to show "out of date" — the dry-run never refreshed the freshness signal. Manual `wl audit-set` was required to make `updatedAt == auditedAt` and restore `isAuditFresh: true`.

## Problem

- `--do-not-persist` is documented as a dry run but gives no freshness guarantee; operators assume a passing validation will clear the stale flag, but it does not.
- Help text (`audit_runner.py:10656`, `10781` and `skill/audit/SKILL.md`) says only "Do not persist the audit report via wl update" — does not explain the Herdr staleness consequence nor the intended dry-run semantics.

## User story

As an operator running `audit_runner.py --do-not-persist` for a dry-run validation, I want a passing validation to still refresh the audit freshness timestamp so Herdr no longer shows the item as out of date, while the full raw report remains not persisted; the flag's help should make this contract explicit.

## Acceptance criteria

1. **Freshness on dry-run success:** When `audit_runner.py issue <id> --do-not-persist` (and `batch --do-not-persist` for each drained item) completes with `Ready to close: Yes`, the work item's `auditedAt` is atomically updated to `now` (`updatedAt == auditedAt` in the same txn, `WL-0MT8KTE3E001Q1D9` pattern) with `auditResult`/`readyToClose` reflecting the verdict, **without** persisting the full `rawOutput` markdown. `isAuditFresh` must be `true` immediately after, and `wl list --stage in_review --json` must show `auditedAt == updatedAt` and `isAuditFresh: true` (Herdr shows ✅ not ⏳ and excludes from audit tier). When the verdict is `Ready to close: No` / `partial` / failure, `auditedAt` is **not** bumped (fail-closed — a failed dry-run must not clear staleness).
2. **Help text updated:** `--do-not-persist` help on both `issue` and `batch` subparsers (and the `SKILL.md` flag table / persistence procedure) is updated to state: dry-run — full audit report is not stored, but on `Ready to close: Yes` the audit freshness timestamp (`auditedAt`/`auditResult`) is still persisted so Herdr/DOWNTIME treat the item as freshly audited; omit the flag to persist the full report. The previous terse "Do not persist the audit report via wl update" is replaced.
3. **No regression for full persist:** Without the flag, behavior is unchanged — full report + `auditedAt`/`auditResult` persisted atomically and lifecycle transitions (`completed`/`in_review` etc.) still apply. With the flag, lifecycle transitions still apply (flag does not suppress status/stage changes).
4. **Tests:** Unit/cli tests cover the new contract: (a) `--do-not-persist` + `Yes` bumps `auditedAt`/`auditResult` but leaves `rawOutput` empty/absent; (b) `--do-not-persist` + `No` does not bump; (c) help text contains the freshness/dry-run wording (mirrors `skill/audit/tests/test_skill_md_and_debug_logs.py` pattern for SKILL.md validation).
5. **Docs:** `skill/audit/SKILL.md` persistence section and runner flag docs updated to match the new flag semantics.

## Notes

- Discovered-from: `SA-0MSJ1BP9K009M8MV` (dry-run left Herdr stale, required manual `wl audit-set` to recover).
- Implementation hint: reuse the atomic `wl audit-set --ready-to-close yes|no` path (sets `updatedAt = auditedAt` in one txn) for the dry-run success case, passing summary but omitting `--raw-output`/`--audit-file` so `rawOutput` stays null. Do not call `wl update --audit-text` afterwards (that would bump `updatedAt` past `auditedAt + 60s` and re-stale).
- `batch` subcommand should apply the same rule per-item in the drain loop.
- Consider whether a new flag (e.g. `--truly-do-not-persist`) is needed for the rare case where even freshness must not be touched; default should be the freshness-preserving dry-run.

## Related work

- `SA-0MSJ1BP9K009M8MV` — effort-and-risk SKILL.md output path (the stale-audit observation)
- `packages/shared/src/icons.ts:isAuditFresh` — `auditedAt > updatedAt - 60s`
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts:selectAuditCandidate` / `isAuditFresh` — audit tier selection
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py:10656,10781` — flag definition
- `skill/audit/scripts/persist_audit.py:495` — atomic `updatedAt = auditedAt` note


## Key Files

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — `--do-not-persist` flag definition and persistence logic
- `skill/audit/scripts/persist_audit.py` — atomic `updatedAt = auditedAt` transaction logic
- `packages/shared/src/icons.ts` — `isAuditFresh()` function
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — `selectAuditCandidate()` / `isAuditFresh` audit tier selection
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md` — runner documentation, flag table, persistence procedure
- `skill/audit/tests/test_skill_md_and_debug_logs.py` — SKILL.md validation test pattern

# Intake Brief: RCA — audit Phase 1 / Phase 2 Reliability

**Work Item:** SA-0MU32H6KY0021SJL

## Headline Summary

Conduct a root cause analysis of why the audit pipeline (Phase 1 screening and Phase 2 deep analysis) frequently fails or degrades, quantify the failure modes from debug logs and stored audit reports, and produce a prioritised set of reliability recommendations with follow-up work items.

## Problem Statement

Audits routinely report `Ready to close: No` for *infrastructure* reasons rather than genuine code defects — concurrency saturation aborting Phase 1 parent screens, wall-clock budget exhaustion silently skipping children, a misleading `parse_failure` debug label that fires on successful calls, and in-main-slot child screens left pending. This forces manual re-audits and blocks releases. No single RCA quantifies these modes or ranks fixes.

## Users

- **Release operator** running an automated audit: needs reliable verdicts without manual re-audits.
- **Producer** reviewing audit results: needs trustworthy signals to make release decisions.
- **Agent** running audits: needs predictable behaviour and actionable failure diagnostics.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A written RCA quantifies failure modes from at least 30 days of evidence, grouped by phase (Phase 1 parent, Phase 1 child, Phase 2 parent deep, Phase 2 child deep, false-positive screen) and by root cause, with reproducible commands/queries and representative examples.
2. The RCA explicitly confirms or refutes **F1** (the `parse_failure` label fires on successful calls) and states the effect on observability; it must distinguish label noise from genuine parse failures.
3. Every failure mode in the RCA is backed by a count and at least one concrete example (item id + log path or report excerpt).
4. A prioritised recommendation list is produced (impact × effort), each item naming the concrete change, the expected reliability effect, and the observable signal that would confirm improvement.
5. Recommendations cover, at minimum: JSON-output contract robustness (e.g. JSON-first prompting / schema retry / fenced-block tolerant parsing), timeout and wall-clock budget right-sizing, concurrency saturation and queue-wait policy, child-audit execution strategy (in-main-slot vs separate-process), provider-error retry policy, and debug-log observability (a correct, non-misleading reason taxonomy).
6. Each accepted recommendation is captured as a follow-up work item (child of this item or `discovered-from`) with its own testable ACs; rejected recommendations record the rationale.
7. UK English throughout; no code changes are required by this item other than producing the RCA/recommendations (implementation lands via the follow-ups).

## Constraints

- Read-only analysis of logs and stored reports; do not modify the audit runner as part of this item.
- Use bounded reads for large log stores (stream, filter by context/reason); never unbounded recursive grep over `.worklog/`.
- Do not close or reopen unrelated work items; link to the prior art below instead.

## Evidence Sources

1. **Debug corpus:** `~/.audit_debug/SorraAgents/audit_debug_*.jsonl` (91 files analysed; raw Pi streams + the logged `reason` field).
2. **Stored audit reports:** `wl show` worklog data (rawOutput per item; counts from 2026-09-15 export).
3. **Runner source:** `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` (`_call_pi`, `_call_pi_and_maybe_log`, `_extract_json_array`, Phase 1/Phase 2 call sites).
4. **Log files:** `~/.audit_debug/SorraAgents/*.log` (audit runs with verdicts and diagnostics).

## Preliminary Findings (to be verified and extended)

### F1 — The debug-log `reason: parse_failure` label is misleading (observability bug)

**Confirmed.** Code inspection of `_call_pi_and_maybe_log` (L4828) shows:

```python
elif isinstance(result, dict) and (result.get("raw_stdout") or result.get("raw_stderr")):
    reason = "provider_error" if result.get("_provider_error") else "parse_failure"
```

The label fires whenever `raw_stdout` or `raw_stderr` is present — which is true on **every** successful call. Corpus analysis of 91 JSONL debug files shows:

- 91 files, all containing `parse_failure` entries as the dominant reason.
- Only 5 files contain `provider_error` (total: ~10 provider_error entries across the corpus).
- Only 2 files contain `debug_log` entries (explicit debug log path was provided).

The preliminary finding of ~92–95% false-positive rate is confirmed — the `parse_failure` label is an observability bug that invalidates any failure analysis keyed on it.

### F2 — Genuine JSON-contract failures are real but rare (~5–8%)

**To be verified.** The preliminary finding cites 34 genuine failures in 285 real-project logs. This count requires verification against the actual debug corpus — checking which `parse_failure` entries actually contain unparseable content vs. parseable content mislabelled by the F1 bug.

### F3 — Wall-clock budget exhaustion dominates (child skips + Phase 2 timeouts)

**Confirmed in log files.** Multiple log entries show:
- "pending deep code review (Phase 1 blocked)" — Phase 2 skipped after Phase 1 detected blocking issues.
- Parent-process timeout budgets vary widely (~120s, 900s, 1500s, 3110s) — inconsistent right-sizing.
- Stored report data (from prior audit): `Skipped due to audit timeout` ~176, `Audit runner skipped this child after Ns` ~100+.

### F4 — Concurrency saturation aborts Phase 1

**Confirmed.** Log files show repeated "Audit concurrency limit reached: audit concurrency queue 'audit' saturated: no slot within 90s" and "Audit concurrency limit reached: semaphore 'audit' busy: no slot free within 0.0s (max_workers=1)". Phase 1 parent screens return `unmet` with zero Pi calls made.

### F5 — In-main-slot child screens leave children unverified

**Confirmed in log files.** Multiple entries show "pending deep code review (Phase 1 blocked)" — child ACs left in `partial (pending main-session review)` state when the main session does not run the emitted `[AUDIT_IN_MAIN_SLOT_WORK]` prompts.

### F6 — Provider errors

**Confirmed.** Corpus analysis: ~10 `provider_error` entries across 91 files (SA-0MSL1Z70C007B9VZ: 3, SA-0MSM6VU2K001IMVP: 1, SA-0MSUT8GQP004WSYN: 1, SA-0MSNYMKV7005P0H9: 1, SA-0MU8EKJYY007PT42: 1). Provider errors are currently conflated with the misleading `parse_failure` label.

## Recommendations (Preliminary — to be finalised)

| Rec | Priority | Impact | Effort | Description | Follow-up Work Item |
|-----|----------|--------|--------|-------------|---------------------|
| R1 | High | High | Low | Fix the debug-log reason taxonomy (observability) | SA-0MU32TAMB007HI99 (R1) |
| R2 | High | High | Medium | Harden JSON contract (JSON-first + tolerant + re-ask) | SA-0MU32TCFM003B78I (R2) |
| R3 | High | High | Medium | Right-size wall-clock budgets; stop silent child skips | SA-0MU32T6O0001UALR (R3) — in_review |
| R4 | High | High | Low-Medium | Priority queue for Phase 1 parent screen | SA-0MU32T8SH001R8MZ (R4) — in_review |
| R5 | Medium-High | High | Low | Enforce child-audit execution contract | SA-0MU32TE120012T49 (R5) |
| R6 | Medium | Medium | Low | Separate provider errors from parse failures | SA-0MU32TFKB0012ALC (R6) — blocked on R1 |
| R7 | Medium | Medium | Low | Emit per-run reliability summary | SA-0MU32TH89000YHP9 (R7) — blocked on R1, R6 |

## Related Work (Prior Art — all evaluated)

| Work Item | Title | Status | Relevance |
|-----------|-------|--------|-----------|
| SA-0MPOGKY8U007K206 | Add debug logging for Pi responses | completed | Introduced current reason label (root of F1) |
| SA-0MQ4GGKUR00752Z8 | Parse JSON array from mixed analysis+JSON | completed | Prior art for JSON contract (R2) |
| SA-0MRW8T054007QH0A | Audit runner bugs | completed | Prior art for JSON parse fallback |
| SA-0MSL1Z15600760KC | Consolidate duplicate Pi JSON parsers | **open, plan_complete** | Should be consulted before R2 implementation |
| SA-0MSF4AFXF000M5DN | Right-size parent-timeout guard | completed | Prior art for budget right-sizing (R3) |
| SA-0MSABZO2T004B95X | Configurable cumulative elapsed-time guard | completed | Prior art for timeout guards |
| SA-0MSGEAZMC009LHKL | Fail immediately on concurrency limit | completed | Prior art superseded by queue admission |
| SA-0MS0SQQTW006GNX9 | Phase 2 deep-analysis timeout | completed | Prior art for timeout issues |
| SA-0MT2XRGEU0009QRE | In-main-slot child audit mode | — | Prior art for R5 |
| SA-0MSQ7MQEJ0064ZB0 | Motivating audit (2026-09-15) | — | Source of this RCA |

## Existing State

The audit runner (`audit_runner.py`) has 10+ call sites for `_call_pi_and_maybe_log`. The debug-log reason taxonomy is set in a single branch (L4906) but is overly broad. The `_extract_json_array` parser exists but does not handle fenced blocks or prose-prefixed JSON consistently. Concurrency is managed via a priority queue with `max_workers=2` (configurable). Wall-clock budgets are set ad-hoc across multiple call sites.

## Desired Change

A comprehensive RCA documenting all failure modes with quantified counts, examples, and reproducible queries — followed by a prioritised recommendation list that feeds into the already-created follow-up work items (R1–R7).

## Key Files (predicted for RCA analysis)

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — All call sites, timeout guards, concurrency, parse logic
- `~/.audit_debug/SorraAgents/audit_debug_*.jsonl` — 91 debug log files (reason taxonomy analysis)
- `~/.audit_debug/SorraAgents/*.log` — 100+ audit run log files (verdict/diagnostic analysis)
- `.worklog/worklog-data.jsonl` — Stored audit reports (rawOutput per item)

## Failure Signature

- Test name: tests/test_cleanup_integration.py::test_cleanup_scripts_dry_run_cli
- Failing commit: 0d0d0fc0ab144e796ce616d8f5436e6a70dd4bed
- CI job: (not available)

## Evidence

- Short stderr/stdout excerpt (first 1k characters):

```
live-repo mutation detected during tests/test_cleanup_integration.py::test_cleanup_scripts_dry_run_cli:
  added config   branch.wl-SA-0MU32TAMB007HI99-r1-audit-debug-log-mislabels-every-succe.merge=refs/heads/dev
  added config   branch.wl-SA-0MU32TAMB007HI99-r1-audit-debug-log-mislabels-every-succe.remote=.
```

## Root Cause (evidence-backed)

The named test is **not defective** — it is the *victim* of a false positive in
the live-repo mutation guard (F5, SA-0MUG30JSE0069JEQ). The guard fails whichever
test finishes next when the main checkout's shared `.git/config` changes mid-run:

- `implement.py::git_worktree_add()` runs `git worktree add --track -b <branch> <path> dev`,
  which writes `branch.<branch>.remote=.` and `branch.<branch>.merge=refs/heads/dev`
  into the **main checkout's shared `.git/config`**.
- `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py::snapshot_repo_state()` captures **all** local config
  (`git config --local --list`).
- `fingerprint()` (`skill/shared/git_sandbox.py:414`) and `diff_snapshots()`
  (`:446-455`) filter agent-worktree **refs** via `excluded_refs`, but do **not**
  filter the matching `branch.<excluded-ref>.{remote,merge}` config keys.
- `live_repo_guard.py::pytest_runtest_teardown` therefore sees a config diff caused
  by a concurrent agent's `implement.py start` and fails the next test to finish —
  here the ~6.7 s cleanup integration test.

This is the same guard false-positive class as SA-0MUILGH5E007X627 (worktree-root
anchoring / ref churn) and SA-0MUII5QDI005U2AH (shared `refs/stash` churn), and
reproduces the root cause first identified for SA-0MUIP4PAG005YI91 (closed as a
false positive without a guard fix).

## Steps To Reproduce

1. Checkout the commit: `git checkout 0d0d0fc0ab144e796ce616d8f5436e6a70dd4bed`
2. Run the failing test: `pytest -q -r a --disable-warnings -k tests/test_cleanup_integration.py::test_cleanup_scripts_dry_run_cli` (or equivalent command)
3. Capture full logs and attach to the work item

## Impact

Failing test detected by agent during automated run. May block PR creation for the agent's current work item. Because the guard misattributes a concurrent
worktree's config churn to an unrelated test, the failure is non-deterministic and
will recur on any shared host with more than one active agent session.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The test `tests/test_cleanup_integration.py::test_cleanup_scripts_dry_run_cli` passes when run against the latest `dev`.
2. The live-repo mutation guard no longer reports a mutation for `branch.<worktree-branch>.remote` / `.merge` config churn written by a concurrent `implement.py start` / worktree registration. Verification: a test mutates the shared `.git/config` branch keys for a branch present in `excluded_refs` and asserts `diff_snapshots(before, after)["changed"] is False` and `fingerprint()` is unchanged.
3. Genuine in-place checkout mutations are still reported (moved `HEAD`/branch ref, tracked-file edit, untracked non-ignored file, unrelated config change); the existing guard contract tests remain green.
4. Documentation describing the guard's exclusion surface (e.g. `docs/dev/test-isolation.md` and the `git_sandbox.py` docstring) is updated to state that worktree-branch config keys are excluded.
5. Full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Related Work

- **SA-0MUILGH5E007X627** — live-repo guard false-positives inside an agent worktree (concurrent worktree ref churn) (open)
- **SA-0MUII5QDI005U2AH** — Live-repo guard: shared refs/stash causes spurious mutation failures across concurrent worktrees (open)
- **SA-0MUIP4PAG005YI91** — same failure signature; closed as a false positive without a guard fix (completed)

## Key Files:

- `tests/test_cleanup_integration.py`
- `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py`
- `skill/shared/live_repo_guard.py`
- `scripts/cleanup/prune_local_branches.py`
- `scripts/cleanup/cleanup_stale_remote_branches.py`
- `docs/dev/test-isolation.md`

## Suggested Triage Steps

1. Verify flakiness: rerun CI/test locally once.
2. If reproducible, assign to `Build` and route for triage.
3. If flaky, tag `flaky` and route to flaky-test queue.

## Suspected Owner

Build (confidence: 0.0, reason: no owner inference available)

## Links

- Runbook: skill/triage/resources/runbook-test-failure.md
- CI artifacts: (not available)

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

Plan skill auto-skip path (effort Extra Small, risk Low): no interactive interview was
run. Questions arising from automated review are recorded below.

- **OPEN QUESTION** (directed to: producer / Build): the guard false-positive class already
  has two open items (SA-0MUILGH5E007X627, SA-0MUII5QDI005U2AH). Should the `branch.<ref>.*`
  config-key filter be implemented here (as AC2 implies), or folded into SA-0MUILGH5E007X627
  as the single shared `git_sandbox.py` fix — with this item then closed as a duplicate symptom?
  Why it matters: proceeding here without a decision risks two divergent fixes to the same helper.
  Recommendation: fold into SA-0MUILGH5E007X627 and close this item as a duplicate, unless the
  producer prefers this item to carry the regression test.
- **Q:** Is the named test itself in scope for change? **Answer (plan review):** no. The test is
  valid; it is only the guard's attribution that is wrong. Evidence: the previous root-cause
  analysis for SA-0MUIP4PAG005YI91 and the reproduction above.

data.description: Full test suites are being launched in overlapping concurrency without any coordination. Current pattern: 3+ concurrent vitest runs each spawning ~16 fork workers at ~400 MB, plus 5+ overlapping pytest/audit runs. This contributes to 566 processes and 1986 threads with load averaging 44 on a 16-core box (3× oversubscription). Solution: implement a global test-job semaphore/queue so only N test suites run simultaneously (suggest N=2), with a config file and a wrapper script (e.g. pace-run.sh) that acquires a lock before launching tests and releases it on completion. Integrate with existing test skills so they use the pacers instead of spawning raw.
